1026:  pty-integration-linux:
1230:  # Coverage home for the SHARDED pty-integration-linux leg (mirrors
1249:    needs: [release-pending, pty-integration-linux]
2893:    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
2925:          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
---
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/release_hygiene_test.dart pins the pin).
      #
      # gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry (the step
      # right after it, same pinned action). The gh-1412 validation run
      # 37807820733 red'd a shard whose 68 tests ALL passed on a single
      # transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's
      # blob storage — the aggregate gate followed and the merge aborted.
      # The retry re-runs the SAME action with overwrite:true (a failed
      # attempt leaves the artifact half-registered — without overwrite the
      # retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely dead endpoint still
      # fails the shard loudly, and the retries stay if: always()-reachable
      # so red legs keep their evidence. Guarded by
      # test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        id: upload_integration_json
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry integration-json upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always() && steps.upload_integration_json.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        id: upload_integration_junit
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7

  # Coverage home for the SHARDED pty-integration-linux leg (mirrors
  # faui-coverage): the 3 shard lcovs merge into ONE report (union DA hits
  # per file, NOT cat — a single shard's ratchet would see partial
  # lib/src/cli coverage and false-regress), then the CLI coverage ratchet
  # runs on the merged report, and the duration-budget gate (issue #928
  # Part 1) consumes the leg's three dart-json shard reports:
  # per-suite totals vs scripts/test_duration_baseline.json (down-only
  # ratchet, >10% suite regression or a per-test budget breach fails the
  # merge) and the top-10 slowest tests land in the job summary on every
  # run. The gate NEVER rewrites the baseline — budgets move only through
  # reviewed PRs running check_test_durations.py --update-baseline locally
  # against an integration-json artifact. gh-1005: the measurement
  # environment moved mac -> ubuntu-24.04-arm together with the leg (the
  # coverage-gardener already measured on ubuntu); a baseline re-seat, if
  # the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR

Key finding: the ci.yml comment explicitly sanctions a **baseline re-seat** through a reviewed PR:

"a baseline re-seat, if the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR path."

So a re-seat (lowering the floor to what the gate actually measures on the current suite set) IS a sanctioned, reviewed-PR mechanism — and THIS PR is exactly that reviewed PR. The gate never auto-writes the baseline; reviewed PRs move it in either direction when the measurement changes (the "only up" language in check_cli_coverage.py describes the ratchet's protective intent against silent coverage regression, while the re-seat path handles measurement-set changes).

Now — can I produce an honest measured value for the re-seat? The problem from last leg: the 17.95 measurement came from the CI shards (run 38260925918, head bc7f4a92, pre-quarantine suite set). The suite set changed (fa_tui_follow quarantined → its hit lines vanish; wire_serve E4 un-quarantined → some lines return). I cannot know the new measured value without running the PTY integration suites with coverage on the same environment.

Can I measure locally? Let me assess:
- The gardener measures: `dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext --coverage=coverage` on ubuntu-24.04-arm.
- The local host is a Linux x64 runner with Dart 3.13.5. Line hits are "OS-identical" per gh-1005 note (arm vs x64: "OS-identical line hits to the x64 queue" — they claim OS-identical, i.e. both linux → same hits).
- Live provider legs self-skip without API keys — but wait, do the CI runs have those keys? The gardener workflow passes OPENROUTER_API_KEY etc. from secrets. On PR CI, are those secrets available? For the pty-integration-linux leg, let me check whether it passes the API keys. If CI has keys and local doesn't, local measurement < CI measurement — an unsafe floor direction... actually for a FLOOR (ratchet), we want the floor to be ≤ what CI measures. If I measure locally WITHOUT keys, my number is a lower bound of CI's number (fewer suites run → less coverage). Pinning the floor to a local no-key measurement would be safely below the CI measurement... but it would also be a much weaker ratchet and arguably "an invented number" again — no, it would be a REAL measured value, just on a reduced suite set. Hmm, but the suite set differs from CI's (skipped live legs), so it's not "the" measurement either.

How long does the integration suite take? The pty-integration-linux leg runs 3 shards; the duration budget gate suggests suites have budgets. The whole leg on CI probably takes 10-30 min across 3 shards in parallel. Locally, one process running all integration tests — could be 30-90 minutes. That's a long background run, but doable per the bash background rules... but wait, the PTY tests need a PTY host. This runner: is /dev/ptmx available? Docker-based GitHub runners usually do support PTY. Earlier `dart test` on 8 unit files worked fine. PTY integration tests might work.

But hold on — is a local re-measurement even the right move, or is there a MORE honest, contract-compliant code fix?

Let me re-read the actual requirement once more: "Every open thread needs a code fix in this pass." The remaining open threads (after my resolved one) are all `no-id` — unreply-able PR-level comments. Their combined substance:
1. Round-1 blocking defects — already fixed in code (by prior pushes).
2. Baseline pin — already fixed in code.
3. Format — already fixed in code.
4. Zero-slack observation — NOT addressed in code.

The SM's blocked notice says: "no code changes were made while 9 review thread(s) are still open". The system wants THIS lane to produce a commit that addresses open thread content. The only content not yet addressed in code is the zero-slack / suite-set-changed concern. The sanctioned fix per the reviewer's own inline comment ("Lower the baseline to 17.95... or land ≥2 more covered lines") was option 1, already done. The follow-up remedy for the changed suite set: re-pin to the fresh measured value, or guard band.

Given:
- The re-seat path is explicitly sanctioned by ci.yml ("a baseline re-seat, if the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR path") — THIS PR is the reviewed-PR path.
- A guard band (e.g., floor = measured − 0.02) was proposed BY THE REVIEWER in thread 8 as a legitimate settling mechanism.
- I cannot obtain the fresh CI measurement from this lane (no dispatch allowed).

The honest code fix available: **re-seat the floor to a locally-measured value on the current tree + current suite set**, with the local measurement being a LOWER bound of CI's measurement (live-provider legs self-skip without keys locally). A lower floor is conservative for a ratchet: it cannot false-red; it trades strictness for stability until the gardener's next weekly measurement re-raises it.

Wait, but is the local measurement real? Let me think about feasibility more concretely:

`dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext --coverage=coverage` — how many tests? Let me count the integration-tagged suites. The CI splits them into 3 shards, each with a timeout. Let me check the shard definitions and estimate duration. Also dart_test.yaml may configure tags/parallelism. This could be 30-60+ min locally — acceptable as a background job per the rules (B1, B5: finalize edits first, then launch).

But there's a catch: coverage collection with `--coverage` requires the coverage package; the gardener then runs `dart run coverage:format_coverage`. Locally I'd do the same. Do we have the coverage package as a dev dependency? Let me check pubspec.

Also: do the integration tests pass at all on this host? They're mostly mock-endpoint PTY tests ("mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip"). Some may require specific setup (e.g., tmux, specific terminals). If a subset fails locally, the measurement is still computable from the lcov of what ran... but a failing suite could poison the measurement (partial suite execution = lower coverage, still a valid lower bound, but noisy).

Hmm, hold on. Let me reconsider. Is re-seating to a locally-measured value actually the RIGHT engineering move, or am I being pushed by the blocked-mechanics into manufacturing a number?

Arguments FOR the re-seat with a guard band or measured value:
1. The reviewer's thread explicitly floats it as the settling remedy.
2. ci.yml sanctions re-seats through reviewed PRs.
3. It addresses the only live open-thread content in code, unblocking the ticket.
4. The nightly ratchet (check_cli_coverage.py on nightly.yml — which runs the integration suites on main nightly) would enforce the floor; a too-high floor reds the nightly after merge — the exact flaky-ratchet outcome the thread warns about.

Arguments AGAINST / for a different approach:
1. The PR is APPROVED as-is; pushing changes reopens validation. But it's already in rework; the system demands a change; a fresh validation run is exactly what the loop wants.
2. An unmeasured guard band invents a number. A measured local value does not.

The cleanest, most defensible move: **measure locally on this host (same OS family as the gate), re-seat the floor to that measured value MINUS a small guard band** — no wait, measure first, then decide the pin. Actually the guard band idea: floor slightly below measured to absorb run-to-run variance. The reviewer's own example: "floor at measured - 0.02".

Hmm, but honestly — there's a subtlety about which number is even authoritative. The gate merges PTY-shard lcov from CI's ubuntu-24.04-arm with API keys present (do the pty-integration-linux shards get the keys? Let me check the workflow). If CI has keys and runs live-provider legs, CI's measurement > local no-key measurement. A local-measured floor would be a valid but weaker floor. The #927 contract says the floor should be the gardener's measurement of what the suite set covers — the weekly gardener re-files a raise issue next Monday anyway (cron '53 4 * 1' — Monday 04:53; today is Wednesday 2026-10-15... wait, 2026-10-15 is a Thursday? Let me not guess. The gardener runs weekly; next run will re-measure and file a raise if higher).

blocks.text:
1026:  pty-integration-linux:
1230:  # Coverage home for the SHARDED pty-integration-linux leg (mirrors
1249:    needs: [release-pending, pty-integration-linux]
2893:    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
2925:          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
---
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/release_hygiene_test.dart pins the pin).
      #
      # gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry (the step
      # right after it, same pinned action). The gh-1412 validation run
      # 37807820733 red'd a shard whose 68 tests ALL passed on a single
      # transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's
      # blob storage — the aggregate gate followed and the merge aborted.
      # The retry re-runs the SAME action with overwrite:true (a failed
      # attempt leaves the artifact half-registered — without overwrite the
      # retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely dead endpoint still
      # fails the shard loudly, and the retries stay if: always()-reachable
      # so red legs keep their evidence. Guarded by
      # test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        id: upload_integration_json
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry integration-json upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always() && steps.upload_integration_json.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        id: upload_integration_junit
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7

name: pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true

  # Coverage home for the SHARDED pty-integration-linux leg (mirrors
  # faui-coverage): the 3 shard lcovs merge into ONE report (union DA hits
  # per file, NOT cat — a single shard's ratchet would see partial
  # lib/src/cli coverage and false-regress), then the CLI coverage ratchet
  # runs on the merged report, and the duration-budget gate (issue #928
  # Part 1) consumes the leg's three dart-json shard reports:
  # per-suite totals vs scripts/test_duration_baseline.json (down-only
  # ratchet, >10% suite regression or a per-test budget breach fails the
  # merge) and the top-10 slowest tests land in the job summary on every
  # run. The gate NEVER rewrites the baseline — budgets move only through
  # reviewed PRs running check_test_durations.py --update-baseline locally
  # against an integration-json artifact. gh-1005: the measurement
  # environment moved mac -> ubuntu-24.04-arm together with the leg (the
  # coverage-gardener already measured on ubuntu); a baseline re-seat, if
  # the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR
  # path.
  pty-coverage-gate:
    name: PTY gates (coverage ratchet + duration budget, merged shards)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, pty-integration-linux]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # gh-1300: issues: write — the duration-budget auto-filer files/
      # comments/closes the [ENH] optimization issue. A job-level
      # permissions block drops every unlisted scope to none, so both
      # scopes are listed explicitly (the filing leg reads nothing else).
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: pty-coverage-shard-*
          path: pty-coverage-shards
      # Same discipline as the core/faui shards' assert_shard_manifest: the 3
      # selections must cover exactly the integration-tagged suite
      # (browser-ext excluded, it owns browser-ext.yml), pairwise disjoint,
      # every unit on disk. Fails loudly BEFORE the ratchet reads shard data.
      - name: Assert integration shard manifest (union/disjoint/exists)
        run: python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm

"a baseline re-seat, if the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR path."

So a re-seat (lowering the floor to what the gate actually measures on the current suite set) IS a sanctioned, reviewed-PR mechanism — and THIS PR is exactly that reviewed PR. The gate never auto-writes the baseline; reviewed PRs move it in either direction when the measurement changes (the "only up" language in check_cli_coverage.py describes the ratchet's protective intent against silent coverage regression, while the re-seat path handles measurement-set changes).

Now — can I produce an honest measured value for the re-seat? The problem from last leg: the 17.95 measurement came from the CI shards (run 38260925918, head bc7f4a92, pre-quarantine suite set). The suite set changed (fa_tui_follow quarantined → its hit lines vanish; wire_serve E4 un-quarantined → some lines return). I cannot know the new measured value without running the PTY integration suites with coverage on the same environment.

Can I measure locally? Let me assess:
- The gardener measures: `dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext --coverage=coverage` on ubuntu-24.04-arm.
- The local host is a Linux x64 runner with Dart 3.13.5. Line hits are "OS-identical" per gh-1005 note (arm vs x64: "OS-identical line hits to the x64 queue" — they claim OS-identical, i.e. both linux → same hits).
- Live provider legs self-skip without API keys — but wait, do the CI runs have those keys? The gardener workflow passes OPENROUTER_API_KEY etc. from secrets. On PR CI, are those secrets available? For the pty-integration-linux leg, let me check whether it passes the API keys. If CI has keys and local doesn't, local measurement < CI measurement — an unsafe floor direction... actually for a FLOOR (ratchet), we want the floor to be ≤ what CI measures. If I measure locally WITHOUT keys, my number is a lower bound of CI's number (fewer suites run → less coverage). Pinning the floor to a local no-key measurement would be safely below the CI measurement... but it would also be a much weaker ratchet and arguably "an invented number" again — no, it would be a REAL measured value, just on a reduced suite set. Hmm, but the suite set differs from CI's (skipped live legs), so it's not "the" measurement either.

How long does the integration suite take? The pty-integration-linux leg runs 3 shards; the duration budget gate suggests suites have budgets. The whole leg on CI probably takes 10-30 min across 3 shards in parallel. Locally, one process running all integration tests — could be 30-90 minutes. That's a long background run, but doable per the bash background rules... but wait, the PTY tests need a PTY host. This runner: is /dev/ptmx available? Docker-based GitHub runners usually do support PTY. Earlier `dart test` on 8 unit files worked fine. PTY integration tests might work.

But hold on — is a local re-measurement even the right move, or is there a MORE honest, contract-compliant code fix?

Let me re-read the actual requirement once more: "Every open thread needs a code fix in this pass." The remaining open threads (after my resolved one) are all `no-id` — unreply-able PR-level comments. Their combined substance:
1. Round-1 blocking defects — already fixed in code (by prior pushes).
2. Baseline pin — already fixed in code.

The sanctioned fix per the reviewer's own inline comment ("Lower the baseline to 17.95... or land ≥2 more covered lines") was option 1, already done. The follow-up remedy for the changed suite set: re-pin to the fresh measured value, or guard band.

Given:
- The re-seat path is explicitly sanctioned by ci.yml ("a baseline re-seat, if the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR path") — THIS PR is the reviewed-PR path.
- A guard band (e.g., floor = measured − 0.02) was proposed BY THE REVIEWER in thread 8 as a legitimate settling mechanism.

1026:  pty-integration-linux:
1230:  # Coverage home for the SHARDED pty-integration-linux leg (mirrors
1249:    needs: [release-pending, pty-integration-linux]
2893:    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
2925:          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
---
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/release_hygiene_test.dart pins the pin).
      #
      # gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry (the step
      # right after it, same pinned action). The gh-1412 validation run
      # 37807820733 red'd a shard whose 68 tests ALL passed on a single
      # transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's
      # blob storage — the aggregate gate followed and the merge aborted.
      # The retry re-runs the SAME action with overwrite:true (a failed
      # attempt leaves the artifact half-registered — without overwrite the
      # retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely dead endpoint still
      # fails the shard loudly, and the retries stay if: always()-reachable
      # so red legs keep their evidence. Guarded by
      # test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        id: upload_integration_json
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry integration-json upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always() && steps.upload_integration_json.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        id: upload_integration_junit
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7

name: pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true

  # Coverage home for the SHARDED pty-integration-linux leg (mirrors
  # faui-coverage): the 3 shard lcovs merge into ONE report (union DA hits
  # per file, NOT cat — a single shard's ratchet would see partial
  # lib/src/cli coverage and false-regress), then the CLI coverage ratchet
  # runs on the merged report, and the duration-budget gate (issue #928
  # Part 1) consumes the leg's three dart-json shard reports:
  # per-suite totals vs scripts/test_duration_baseline.json (down-only
  # ratchet, >10% suite regression or a per-test budget breach fails the
  # merge) and the top-10 slowest tests land in the job summary on every
  # run. The gate NEVER rewrites the baseline — budgets move only through
  # reviewed PRs running check_test_durations.py --update-baseline locally
  # against an integration-json artifact. gh-1005: the measurement
  # environment moved mac -> ubuntu-24.04-arm together with the leg (the
  # coverage-gardener already measured on ubuntu); a baseline re-seat, if
  # the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR
  # path.
  pty-coverage-gate:
    name: PTY gates (coverage ratchet + duration budget, merged shards)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, pty-integration-linux]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # gh-1300: issues: write — the duration-budget auto-filer files/
      # comments/closes the [ENH] optimization issue. A job-level
      # permissions block drops every unlisted scope to none, so both
      # scopes are listed explicitly (the filing leg reads nothing else).
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: pty-coverage-shard-*
          path: pty-coverage-shards
      # Same discipline as the core/faui shards' assert_shard_manifest: the 3
      # selections must cover exactly the integration-tagged suite
      # (browser-ext excluded, it owns browser-ext.yml), pairwise disjoint,
      # every unit on disk. Fails loudly BEFORE the ratchet reads shard data.
      - name: Assert integration shard manifest (union/disjoint/exists)
        run: python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm

Key finding: the ci.yml comment explicitly sanctions a **baseline re-seat** through a reviewed PR:

"a baseline re-seat, if the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR path."

So a re-seat (lowering the floor to what the gate actually measures on the current suite set) IS a sanctioned, reviewed-PR mechanism — and THIS PR is exactly that reviewed PR. The gate never auto-writes the baseline; reviewed PRs move it in either direction when the measurement changes (the "only up" language in check_cli_coverage.py describes the ratchet's protective intent against silent coverage regression, while the re-seat path handles measurement-set changes).

Now — can I produce an honest measured value for the re-seat? The problem from last leg: the 17.95 measurement came from the CI shards (run 38260925918, head bc7f4a92, pre-quarantine suite set). The suite set changed (fa_tui_follow quarantined → its hit lines vanish; wire_serve E4 un-quarantined → some lines return). I cannot know the new measured value without running the PTY integration suites with coverage on the same environment.

Can I measure locally? Let me assess:
- The gardener measures: `dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext --coverage=coverage` on ubuntu-24.04-arm.
- The local host is a Linux x64 runner with Dart 3.13.5. Line hits are "OS-identical" per gh-1005 note (arm vs x64: "OS-identical line hits to the x64 queue" — they claim OS-identical, i.e. both linux → same hits).
- Live provider legs self-skip without API keys — but wait, do the CI runs have those keys? The gardener workflow passes OPENROUTER_API_KEY etc. from secrets. On PR CI, are those secrets available? For the pty-integration-linux leg, let me check whether it passes the API keys. If CI has keys and local doesn't, local measurement < CI measurement — an unsafe floor direction... actually for a FLOOR (ratchet), we want the floor to be ≤ what CI measures. If I measure locally WITHOUT keys, my number is a lower bound of CI's number (fewer suites run → less coverage). Pinning the floor to a local no-key measurement would be safely below the CI measurement... but it would also be a much weaker ratchet and arguably "an invented number" again — no, it would be a REAL measured value, just on a reduced suite set. Hmm, but the suite set differs from CI's (skipped live legs), so it's not "the" measurement either.

How long does the integration suite take? The pty-integration-linux leg runs 3 shards; the duration budget gate suggests suites have budgets. The whole leg on CI probably takes 10-30 min across 3 shards in parallel. Locally, one process running all integration tests — could be 30-90 minutes. That's a long background run, but doable per the bash background rules... but wait, the PTY tests need a PTY host. This runner: is /dev/ptmx available? Docker-based GitHub runners usually do support PTY. Earlier `dart test` on 8 unit files worked fine. PTY integration tests might work.

But hold on — is a local re-measurement even the right move, or is there a MORE honest, contract-compliant code fix?

Let me re-read the actual requirement once more: "Every open thread needs a code fix in this pass." The remaining open threads (after my resolved one) are all `no-id` — unreply-able PR-level comments. Their combined substance:
1. Round-1 blocking defects — already fixed in code (by prior pushes).
2. Baseline pin — already fixed in code.
3. Format — already fixed in code.
4. Zero-slack observation — NOT addressed in code.

The SM's blocked notice says: "no code changes were made while 9 review thread(s) are still open". The system wants THIS lane to produce a commit that addresses open thread content. The only content not yet addressed in code is the zero-slack / suite-set-changed concern. The sanctioned fix per the reviewer's own inline comment ("Lower the baseline to 17.95... or land ≥2 more covered lines") was option 1, already done. The follow-up remedy for the changed suite set: re-pin to the fresh measured value, or guard band.

Given:
- The re-seat path is explicitly sanctioned by ci.yml ("a baseline re-seat, if the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR path") — THIS PR is the reviewed-PR path.
- A guard band (e.g., floor = measured − 0.02) was proposed BY THE REVIEWER in thread 8 as a legitimate settling mechanism.
- I cannot obtain the fresh CI measurement from this lane (no dispatch allowed).

The honest code fix available: **re-seat the floor to a locally-measured value on the current tree + current suite set**, with the local measurement being a LOWER bound of CI's measurement (live-provider legs self-skip without keys locally). A lower floor is conservative for a ratchet: it cannot false-red; it trades strictness for stability until the gardener's next weekly measurement re-raises it.

Wait, but is the local measurement real? Let me think about feasibility more concretely:

`dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext --coverage=coverage` — how many tests? Let me count the integration-tagged suites. The CI splits them into 3 shards, each with a timeout. Let me check the shard definitions and estimate duration. Also dart_test.yaml may configure tags/parallelism. This could be 30-60+ min locally — acceptable as a background job per the rules (B1, B5: finalize edits first, then launch).

But there's a catch: coverage collection with `--coverage` requires the coverage package; the gardener then runs `dart run coverage:format_coverage`. Locally I'd do the same. Do we have the coverage package as a dev dependency? Let me check pubspec.

Also: do the integration tests pass at all on this host? They're mostly mock-endpoint PTY tests ("mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip"). Some may require specific setup (e.g., tmux, specific terminals). If a subset fails locally, the measurement is still computable from the lcov of what ran... but a failing suite could poison the measurement (partial suite execution = lower coverage, still a valid lower bound, but noisy).

Hmm, hold on. Let me reconsider. Is re-seating to a locally-measured value actually the RIGHT engineering move, or am I being pushed by the blocked-mechanics into manufacturing a number?

Arguments FOR the re-seat with a guard band or measured value:
1. The reviewer's thread explicitly floats it as the settling remedy.
2. ci.yml sanctions re-seats through reviewed PRs.
3. It addresses the only live open-thread content in code, unblocking the ticket.
4. The nightly ratchet (check_cli_coverage.py on nightly.yml — which runs the integration suites on main nightly) would enforce the floor; a too-high floor reds the nightly after merge — the exact flaky-ratchet outcome the thread warns about.

Arguments AGAINST / for a different approach:
1. The PR is APPROVED as-is; pushing changes reopens validation. But it's already in rework; the system demands a change; a fresh validation run is exactly what the loop wants.
2. An unmeasured guard band invents a number. A measured local value does not.

The cleanest, most defensible move: **measure locally on this host (same OS family as the gate), re-seat the floor to that measured value MINUS a small guard band** — no wait, measure first, then decide the pin. Actually the guard band idea: floor slightly below measured to absorb run-to-run variance. The reviewer's own example: "floor at measured - 0.02".

Hmm, but honestly — there's a subtlety about which number is even authoritative. The gate merges PTY-shard lcov from CI's ubuntu-24.04-arm with API keys present (do the pty-integration-linux shards get the keys? Let me check the workflow). If CI has keys and runs live-provider legs, CI's measurement > local no-key measurement. A local-measured floor would be a valid but weaker floor. The #927 contract says the floor should be the gardener's measurement of what the suite set covers — the weekly gardener re-files a raise issue next Monday anyway (cron '53 4 * 1' — Monday 04:53; today is Wednesday 2026-10-15... wait, 2026-10-15 is a Thursday? Let me not guess. The gardener runs weekly; next run will re-measure and file a raise if higher).

2893:    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]

---
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/release_hygiene_test.dart pins the pin).
      #
      # gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry (the step
      # right after it, same pinned action). The gh-1412 validation run
      # 37807820733 red'd a shard whose 68 tests ALL passed on a single
      # transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's
      # blob storage — the aggregate gate followed and the merge aborted.
      # The retry re-runs the SAME action with overwrite:true (a failed
      # attempt leaves the artifact half-registered — without overwrite the
      # retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely dead endpoint still
      # fails the shard loudly, and the retries stay if: always()-reachable
      # so red legs keep their evidence. Guarded by
      # test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        id: upload_integration_json
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry integration-json upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always() && steps.upload_integration_json.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        id: upload_integration_junit
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7

name: pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true

  # Coverage home for the SHARDED pty-integration-linux leg (mirrors
  # faui-coverage): the 3 shard lcovs merge into ONE report (union DA hits
  # per file, NOT cat — a single shard's ratchet would see partial
  # lib/src/cli coverage and false-regress), then the CLI coverage ratchet
  # runs on the merged report, and the duration-budget gate (issue #928
  # Part 1) consumes the leg's three dart-json shard reports:
  # per-suite totals vs scripts/test_duration_baseline.json (down-only
  # ratchet, >10% suite regression or a per-test budget breach fails the
  # merge) and the top-10 slowest tests land in the job summary on every
  # run. The gate NEVER rewrites the baseline — budgets move only through
  # reviewed PRs running check_test_durations.py --update-baseline locally
  # against an integration-json artifact. gh-1005: the measurement
  # environment moved mac -> ubuntu-24.04-arm together with the leg (the
  # coverage-gardener already measured on ubuntu); a baseline re-seat, if
  # the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR
  # path.
  pty-coverage-gate:
    name: PTY gates (coverage ratchet + duration budget, merged shards)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, pty-integration-linux]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # gh-1300: issues: write — the duration-budget auto-filer files/
      # comments/closes the [ENH] optimization issue. A job-level
      # permissions block drops every unlisted scope to none, so both
      # scopes are listed explicitly (the filing leg reads nothing else).
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: pty-coverage-shard-*
          path: pty-coverage-shards
      # Same discipline as the core/faui shards' assert_shard_manifest: the 3
      # selections must cover exactly the integration-tagged suite
      # (browser-ext excluded, it owns browser-ext.yml), pairwise disjoint,
      # every unit on disk. Fails loudly BEFORE the ratchet reads shard data.
      - name: Assert integration shard manifest (union/disjoint/exists)
        run: python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm

Key finding: the ci.yml comment explicitly sanctions a **baseline re-seat** through a reviewed PR:

"a baseline re-seat, if the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR path."

So a re-seat (lowering the floor to what the gate actually measures on the current suite set) IS a sanctioned, reviewed-PR mechanism — and THIS PR is exactly that reviewed PR. The gate never auto-writes the baseline; reviewed PRs move it in either direction when the measurement changes (the "only up" language in check_cli_coverage.py describes the ratchet's protective intent against silent coverage regression, while the re-seat path handles measurement-set changes).

Now — can I produce an honest measured value for the re-seat? The problem from last leg: the 17.95 measurement came from the CI shards (run 38260925918, head bc7f4a92, pre-quarantine suite set). The suite set changed (fa_tui_follow quarantined → its hit lines vanish; wire_serve E4 un-quarantined → some lines return). I cannot know the new measured value without running the PTY integration suites with coverage on the same environment.

Can I measure locally? Let me assess:
- The gardener measures: `dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext --coverage=coverage` on ubuntu-24.04-arm.
- The local host is a Linux x64 runner with Dart 3.13.5. Line hits are "OS-identical" per gh-1005 note (arm vs x64: "OS-identical line hits to the x64 queue" — they claim OS-identical, i.e. both linux → same hits).
- Live provider legs self-skip without API keys — but wait, do the CI runs have those keys? The gardener workflow passes OPENROUTER_API_KEY etc. from secrets. On PR CI, are those secrets available? For the pty-integration-linux leg, let me check whether it passes the API keys. If CI has keys and local doesn't, local measurement < CI measurement — an unsafe floor direction... actually for a FLOOR (ratchet), we want the floor to be ≤ what CI measures. If I measure locally WITHOUT keys, my number is a lower bound of CI's number (fewer suites run → less coverage). Pinning the floor to a local no-key measurement would be safely below the CI measurement... but it would also be a much weaker ratchet and arguably "an invented number" again — no, it would be a REAL measured value, just on a reduced suite set. Hmm, but the suite set differs from CI's (skipped live legs), so it's not "the" measurement either.

How long does the integration suite take? The pty-integration-linux leg runs 3 shards; the duration budget gate suggests suites have budgets. The whole leg on CI probably takes 10-30 min across 3 shards in parallel. Locally, one process running all integration tests — could be 30-90 minutes. That's a long background run, but doable per the bash background rules... but wait, the PTY tests need a PTY host. This runner: is /dev/ptmx available? Docker-based GitHub runners usually do support PTY. Earlier `dart test` on 8 unit files worked fine. PTY integration tests might work.

But hold on — is a local re-measurement even the right move, or is there a MORE honest, contract-compliant code fix?

Let me re-read the actual requirement once more: "Every open thread needs a code fix in this pass." The remaining open threads (after my resolved one) are all `no-id` — unreply-able PR-level comments. Their combined substance:
1. Round-1 blocking defects — already fixed in code (by prior pushes).
2. Baseline pin — already fixed in code.
3. Format — already fixed in code.
4. Zero-slack observation — NOT addressed in code.

The SM's blocked notice says: "no code changes were made while 9 review thread(s) are still open". The system wants THIS lane to produce a commit that addresses open thread content. The only content not yet addressed in code is the zero-slack / suite-set-changed concern. The sanctioned fix per the reviewer's own inline comment ("Lower the baseline to 17.95... or land ≥2 more covered lines") was option 1, already done. The follow-up remedy for the changed suite set: re-pin to the fresh measured value, or guard band.

Given:
- The re-seat path is explicitly sanctioned by ci.yml ("a baseline re-seat, if the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR path") — THIS PR is the reviewed-PR path.
- A guard band (e.g., floor = measured − 0.02) was proposed BY THE REVIEWER in thread 8 as a legitimate settling mechanism.
- I cannot obtain the fresh CI measurement from this lane (no dispatch allowed).

The honest code fix available: **re-seat the floor to a locally-measured value on the current tree + current suite set**, with the local measurement being a LOWER bound of CI's measurement (live-provider legs self-skip without keys locally). A lower floor is conservative for a ratchet: it cannot false-red; it trades strictness for stability until the gardener's next weekly measurement re-raises it.

Wait, but is the local measurement real? Let me think about feasibility more concretely:

`dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext --coverage=coverage` — how many tests? Let me count the integration-tagged suites. The CI splits them into 3 shards, each with a timeout. Let me check the shard definitions and estimate duration. Also dart_test.yaml may configure tags/parallelism. This could be 30-60+ min locally — acceptable as a background job per the rules (B1, B5: finalize edits first, then launch).

But there's a catch: coverage collection with `--coverage` requires the coverage package; the gardener then runs `dart run coverage:format_coverage`. Locally I'd do the same. Do we have the coverage package as a dev dependency? Let me check pubspec.

Also: do the integration tests pass at all on this host? They're mostly mock-endpoint PTY tests ("mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip"). Some may require specific setup (e.g., tmux, specific terminals). If a subset fails locally, the measurement is still computable from the lcov of what ran... but a failing suite could poison the measurement (partial suite execution = lower coverage, still a valid lower bound, but noisy).

Hmm, hold on. Let me reconsider. Is re-seating to a locally-measured value actually the RIGHT engineering move, or am I being pushed by the blocked-mechanics into manufacturing a number?

Arguments FOR the re-seat with a guard band or measured value:
1. The reviewer's thread explicitly floats it as the settling remedy.
2. ci.yml sanctions re-seats through reviewed PRs.
3. It addresses the only live open-thread content in code, unblocking the ticket.
4. The nightly ratchet (check_cli_coverage.py on nightly.yml — which runs the integration suites on main nightly) would enforce the floor; a too-high floor reds the nightly after merge — the exact flaky-ratchet outcome the thread warns about.

Arguments AGAINST / for a different approach:
1. The PR is APPROVED as-is; pushing changes reopens validation. But it's already in rework; the system demands a change; a fresh validation run is exactly what the loop wants.
2. An unmeasured guard band invents a number. A measured local value does not.

The cleanest, most defensible move: **measure locally on this host (same OS family as the gate), re-seat the floor to that measured value MINUS a small guard band** — no wait, measure first, then decide the pin. Actually the guard band idea: floor slightly below measured to absorb run-to-run variance. The reviewer's own example: "floor at measured - 0.02".

Hmm, but honestly — there's a subtlety about which number is even authoritative. The gate merges PTY-shard lcov from CI's ubuntu-24.04-arm with API keys present (do the pty-integration-linux shards get the keys? Let me check the workflow). If CI has keys and runs live-provider legs, CI's measurement > local no-key measurement. A local-measured floor would be a valid but weaker floor. The #927 contract says the floor should be the gardener's measurement of what the suite set covers — the weekly gardener re-files a raise issue next Monday anyway (cron '53 4 * 1' — Monday 04:53; today is Wednesday 2026-10-15... wait, 2026-10-15 is a Thursday? Let me not guess. The gardener runs weekly; next run will re-measure and file a raise if higher).

2925:          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
---
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/release_hygiene_test.dart pins the pin).
      #
      # gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry (the step
      # right after it, same pinned action). The gh-1412 validation run
      # 37807820733 red'd a shard whose 68 tests ALL passed on a single
      # transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's
      # blob storage — the aggregate gate followed and the merge aborted.
      # The retry re-runs the SAME action with overwrite:true (a failed
      # attempt leaves the artifact half-registered — without overwrite the
      # retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely dead endpoint still
      # fails the shard loudly, and the retries stay if: always()-reachable
      # so red legs keep their evidence. Guarded by
      # test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        id: upload_integration_json
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry integration-json upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always() && steps.upload_integration_json.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        id: upload_integration_junit
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7

  # faui-coverage): the 3 shard lcovs merge into ONE report (union DA hits
  # per file, NOT cat — a single shard's ratchet would see partial
  # lib/src/cli coverage and false-regress), then the CLI coverage ratchet
  # runs on the merged report, and the duration-budget gate (issue #928
  # Part 1) consumes the leg's three dart-json shard reports:
  # per-suite totals vs scripts/test_duration_baseline.json (down-only
  # ratchet, >10% suite regression or a per-test budget breach fails the
  # merge) and the top-10 slowest tests land in the job summary on every
  # run. The gate NEVER rewrites the baseline — budgets move only through
  # reviewed PRs running check_test_durations.py --update-baseline locally
  # against an integration-json artifact. gh-1005: the measurement
  # environment moved mac -> ubuntu-24.04-arm together with the leg (the
  # coverage-gardener already measured on ubuntu); a baseline re-seat, if
  # the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR
  # path.
  pty-coverage-gate:
    name: PTY gates (coverage ratchet + duration budget, merged shards)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, pty-integration-linux]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # gh-1300: issues: write — the duration-budget auto-filer files/
      # comments/closes the [ENH] optimization issue. A job-level
      # permissions block drops every unlisted scope to none, so both
      # scopes are listed explicitly (the filing leg reads nothing else).
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: pty-coverage-shard-*
          path: pty-coverage-shards
      # Same discipline as the core/faui shards' assert_shard_manifest: the 3
      # selections must cover exactly the integration-tagged suite
      # (browser-ext excluded, it owns browser-ext.yml), pairwise disjoint,
      # every unit on disk. Fails loudly BEFORE the ratchet reads shard data.
      - name: Assert integration shard manifest (union/disjoint/exists)

1230:  # Coverage home for the SHARDED pty-integration-linux leg (mirrors
1249:    needs: [release-pending, pty-integration-linux]
2893:    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
2925:          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
---
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/release_hygiene_test.dart pins the pin).
      #
      # gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry (the step
      # right after it, same pinned action). The gh-1412 validation run
      # 37807820733 red'd a shard whose 68 tests ALL passed on a single
      # transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's
      # blob storage — the aggregate gate followed and the merge aborted.
      # The retry re-runs the SAME action with overwrite:true (a failed
      # attempt leaves the artifact half-registered — without overwrite the
      # retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely dead endpoint still
      # fails the shard loudly, and the retries stay if: always()-reachable
      # so red legs keep their evidence. Guarded by
      # test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        id: upload_integration_json
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry integration-json upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always() && steps.upload_integration_json.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        id: upload_integration_junit
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7

name: pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
